resources.string: Umukino w\'Ubwenge • Royal Strategy of Rwanda
Ndakubye! Opponent retreated front-row seeds to the back row.
Your final seed landed in an occupied inner pit directly opposite two occupied opponent pits. Do you want to capture (Kurasa) or pass (Ndahise)?
“Ubwenge burarahurwa.”\nWisdom is kindled from one mind to another.
“Uhagaraye amaguru abiri abona kure.”\nOne who plans with foresight sees far ahead.
“Umutwe umwe ntiwigira inama.”\nA single head alone cannot take full counsel.

Each player commands 2 rows of 8 pits (16 pits total) starting with 32 Inka (seeds)—4 in each back-row pit. Select any pit on your side containing at least 2 seeds and sow them one by one counter-clockwise around your 16 pits. Pits with only 1 seed cannot initiate a move.

If the final seed in your hand drops into an already occupied pit (without triggering a capture), you immediately scoop up all seeds from that pit and continue sowing in a relay loop. Your turn only ends when your final seed drops into an empty pit.

If your last seed lands in an occupied pit in your inner row AND both of your opponent\'s opposite pits in that same column contain at least 1 seed, you capture all seeds from both opponent pits! You immediately resow the captured seeds starting from the pit where the capturing lap began.

In traditional Rwandan play, capturing is optional. If you decline a capture by declaring “Ndahise” (I pass), your opponent may respond “Ndakubye” (I retreat), immediately moving their front-row seeds in that column into their back-row pit so the column can no longer be captured.
